name: Shoko
description:
**Personal fork** of [Shokofin](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/Shokofin). It may not be maintained or well-tested. See [crowquillx/Shokofin](https://github.com/crowquillx/Shokofin).
A Jellyfin plugin to integrate [Jellyfin](https://jellyfin.org/docs/) with [Shoko Server](https://shokoanime.com/downloads/shoko-server/).
## Read this before installing
**This plugin requires that you have already set up and are using Shoko Server**, and that the files you intend to include in Jellyfin are **indexed** (and optionally managed) by Shoko Server. **Otherwise, the plugin won't be able to provide metadata for your files**, since there is no metadata to find for them.
overview: Manage your anime from Jellyfin using metadata from Shoko (personal fork)

versions.changelog:
Only compatible with **12.y.z**.

See the [release notes](https://github.com/crowquillx/Shokofin/releases/tag/v6.1.0-dev.2) for more info.

---

`fix`: **Create the TheIntroDB segment provider without loading Shoko services**:

Jellyfin creates media segment providers while it starts, before it loads
plugins. The provider took ShokoApiManager and ShokoIdLookup in its
constructor, which created ShokoApiClient, whose constructor reads
Plugin.Instance.Configuration while Plugin.Instance is still null. The
NullReferenceException aborted Jellyfin's startup (6.1.0.1 on Jellyfin 12.4).

The provider now takes the service provider and looks those services up on
first use, and treats a missing Plugin.Instance as disabled.

The release workflows now start a fresh Jellyfin for each built zip (10.10.7,
10.11.11 and 12) and refuse to publish unless it becomes healthy with the
plugin loaded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`fix`: **Skip placeholder and made-up episode titles**:

Treat "TBA", "TBD", "To be announced" and decimal "Episode 12.5" titles as
placeholders, and skip the names daily Shoko makes up for episodes with no
AniDB title (e.g. "第12話") so the next title provider, such as TMDB, is
used. The made-up name is still used when no provider has a real title.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`feat`: **Add an option to shorten season titles**:

With "Shorten Season Titles" on (off by default), seasons in shows with
several seasons drop the show's title from the front, so "Demon Slayer:
Entertainment District Arc" becomes "Entertainment District Arc". A season
keeps its full title when only a year, a number or a few characters would be
left, every season keeps it when fewer than half start with the show's
title, and seasons with the same title are told apart by their AniDB main
title. Ported from the Silo ShokoAnime VFS plugin. Does not apply to the TMDB
structure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`feat`: **Add a TheIntroDB media segment provider that uses Shoko's TMDB links**:

Add a "TheIntroDB (Shoko)" media segment provider. A Shokofin episode is
numbered by its place in the Shoko series or group, which often is not
TMDB's numbering, so the provider looks an episode up by the TMDB episode
Shoko links it to, in that show's default order, and a movie by its linked
TMDB movie. Items without a TMDB link get no segments.

Credits and previews are kept only when TheIntroDB timed them on a release
within 5 minutes of the file's length; intros and recaps are kept either
way. Lookups are paced (400 ms anonymous, 100 ms with an API key), cached,
shared between concurrent callers, and paused when TheIntroDB asks clients
to back off. Nothing is ever submitted. On Jellyfin 10.11+ a failed lookup
keeps the provider's existing segments, and an item that already has an
intro and an outro is not looked up again unless refreshed with overwrite.

The provider is off by default; enable it and optionally set an API key
under Metadata settings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`feat`: **Use Season Posters show posters and warn about restricted tags**:

Read the show poster list of the Season Posters Shoko plugin
(GET /api/plugin/season-posters/show-posters) and put the chosen show poster
first for shows built from Shoko groups, and the chosen specials poster first
for their specials season. Keys map to Shokofin's Shoko group structure:
`group:<id>` for a group without sub-groups, `series:<id>` for a series shown
on its own; Silo-only entries are skipped. The list is cached for 10 minutes,
and a Shoko server without the plugin, or a failed lookup, leaves images as
they were. On by default (SeasonPosters_Enabled).

Also check the Shoko user the API key belongs to (GET /api/v3/User/Current)
and, when Shoko hides tags from it, log a warning on connect and show it on
the connection tab, since every series with one of those tags is missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`feat`: **Follow more Shoko events and catch up after a lost connection**:

Listen for the Shoko Server events Shokofin ignored:

- file:hashed / ShokoEvent:FileHashed: re-read a hashed file that already
  has episodes. A file whose contents Shoko already knew keeps its stored
  release and gets no match event.
- ShokoEvent:FileNotMatched and file:updated (ignored/variation changes):
  re-read the file.
- release:removed / release:deleted: re-read the file, which removes its
  links now that it has no episodes.
- metadata:{series,episode,movie}.image{Added,Updated,Removed}: daily
  servers name image events after their reason, so they never reached the
  existing image refresh.
- group:group.*, group:series.moved, group:recreated (daily, new group
  feed): clear the cached show data, link the files of the affected series
  again and refresh their shows; a recreate scans the libraries.
- metadata:links.changed, metadata:episode.hiddenChanged,
  metadata:series.customTagsChanged: link the affected series' files again
  and refresh their shows.

Shoko does not replay events sent while we were not listening, so after the
connection is lost and comes back, scan the libraries with file or refresh
events enabled once (debounced, at most every 10 minutes). An optional
periodic scan can be turned on in the SignalR settings.

New settings: SignalR_CatchUpOnReconnect (default on) and
SignalR_PeriodicCatchUpIntervalInHours (default 0, off).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`misc`: **Feat(vfs): keep and share theme songs, optionally leave out covered variations**:

The VFS cleanup removed every audio file it had not generated unless it sat
in a `theme-music` folder below a show, so a `theme.mp3` that a theme song
plugin downloads into a VFS show or season folder was deleted on the next
VFS generation. Theme songs without Shoko IDs (`theme.<ext>`,
`theme<N>.<ext>`, and audio in `theme-music`, `theme-songs`, `themes`,
`theme songs` or `theme music` folders) are now kept while their show or
season is in the VFS, follow their show when its folder is renamed, and are
removed with it otherwise. Links to theme songs that are gone are removed,
but only while their media folder can be read. On by default
(`VFS_PreserveThemeSongs`).

`VFS_SyncThemeSongs` (off by default) shares theme songs with the media
folders on full VFS generations. A media folder is paired with a VFS show or
season only when every file in it belongs to that show (or that season's
series) and it is not a media folder root. Its theme songs are linked into
the VFS, and theme songs written into the VFS are copied into the media
folder's theme folder (or a new `theme-music` folder) and replaced with a
link to the copy. Nothing in a media folder is overwritten or removed; name
clashes are logged.

`VFS_SkipCoveredVariations` (off by default) leaves out files Shoko marks as
a variation for episodes that a file which is not a variation already
covers. Variations are held back until every other file has been seen, so a
variation that is an episode's only file, such as one part of an episode
split across files, is kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
